question: Do we have a rule about indexing foreign keys, or was it already done?
source: supabase/migrations/20261009180000_index_foreign_keys.sql (DB-IDX-1); docs/decisions/data.md → 2026-10-22 "DB-PERF-1: an advisor's 'unused index' is not a reason to drop…"
gold: It was done: migration 20261009180000_index_foreign_keys (DB-IDX-1) added a btree index for every foreign key the advisor flagged as unindexed. The standing rule is DB-PERF-1 (2026-10-22): drop an index only when it is provably redundant, and never when it is the only one covering an FK; an advisor's unused-index verdict is no evidence on a small database.
staleAnswer: It was done in DB-IDX-1, but there is no standing rule about foreign-key indexes.

question: Does a release push every pending migration to prod?

question: How do we resolve a migration-filename collision or a migration history mismatch?
source: docs/decisions/data.md → 2026-07-29 "A migration-filename collision is resolved by re-stamping the idempotent file…"; .claude/rules/supabase.md
gold: Re-stamp the file of the pair whose SQL is provably re-runnable (ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS and the like), choosing a stamp that replays prod's real apply order from list_migrations rather than filenames, then grep the docs for the old stamp. migration-order.test.ts fails verify on a collision; check open PRs' migrations before picking a stamp.

question: Do internal SECURITY DEFINER helpers need EXECUTE revoked from authenticated?

gold: Yes. A helper only other definer functions call gets REVOKE ALL … FROM PUBLIC, anon, authenticated and GRANT EXECUTE … TO service_role, named with a double underscore, and has_function_privilege is asserted for both client roles; REVOKE FROM PUBLIC alone leaves anon able to execute. Exceptions keep client EXECUTE: policy helpers, app RPCs and functions a CHECK, policy or trigger calls.
staleAnswer: No: revoking from PUBLIC is enough, authenticated can keep EXECUTE. Only public is enough for internal helpers.

question: What breaks under the React Compiler when a hook reads a mutable store during render?
source: docs/gotchas/ui.md → React effects ("With the React Compiler on… must RETURN the useSyncExternalStore snapshot")
gold: The compiler memoises a store.read(ref) call made next to useSyncExternalStore(subscribe, getVersion), so the component re-renders but keeps a stale value (RF-1's useReference stuck on Loading). Return the snapshot itself — useSyncExternalStore(subscribe, () => store.read(ref)). rstest builds without the compiler, so unit tests don't catch it.

question: Can we trust the sender identity of a Realtime broadcast in notes?
source: docs/gotchas/notes.md → Agent writes (NR-6) ("Never trust 'who wrote this' from a broadcast")
gold: No. Realtime checks policies only at join, so a payload can carry anything, and since NR-7 clients can't send on notes at all. Agent writes are announced content-free ({ pull: true } from the note_updates trigger); the stored row, written server-side from module_api_key_id(), is the only source of who wrote it.

question: After NR-7, do clients broadcast who is viewing a note?
source: docs/decisions/notes.md → 2026-10-16 "NR-7 built — clients send nothing over Realtime…"
gold: No. Clients send nothing over Realtime. Presence is a server heartbeat, notes_live_here every 20 s, which checks view access and records the tab in note_live_viewers; the server sends the viewer list on each person's own private read-only topic notes-live:<uid>.
staleAnswer: Yes, each client calls presence.track() on the note's channel and clients broadcast presence with their name.

question: Why did note Realtime move to a private per-note channel?
source: specs/notes-refresh.md → Assumptions & technical decisions, item 18 "Secure channel (revised while building NR-7…)"; docs/decisions/notes.md 2026-10-16 NR-7
gold: It didn't end up per-note. The public notes:<id> relay let anyone forge bytes; a per-note private topic was rejected while building NR-7 because Realtime checks policies only at join (a revoked listener keeps hearing) and can't see payloads. Instead each person listens on one private read-only topic, notes-live:<uid>, and the server sends content-free pull messages to the current viewers.
staleAnswer: Each note gets its own private channel, note:<id>, with private: true and an RLS policy on realtime.messages: read needs view and send needs edit.
